issues.legal_issue: Contemporaneous corroboration and consistent eyewitness testimony can establish the witnesses’ presence and support reliance on their account.
material_facts: The prosecution relied on two eyewitnesses, one of whom was the deceased’s companion and the other her brother.
A railway official sent a telegram within an hour of the incident stating that the companion had reported the killing at the scene.
The court assessed both witnesses’ evidence and found it reliable.
issues.conclusion: The court rejected the challenge to the witnesses’ presence and held that their testimony could safely be relied upon.
issues.legal_principle: The court assessed the eyewitness evidence in light of the contemporaneous telegram, which corroborated a witness’s presence at the scene. No earlier cases or particular statutory provisions were relied on for this issue.

predicates.appeal_from_conviction: The accused appealed from convictions entered by the lower courts.
predicates.contemporaneous_report_identified_witnes: A report made shortly after the incident recorded that a witness had informed an official about the event at the scene.
predicates.eyewitness_accounts_assessed_as_reliable: The court assessed the eyewitness accounts and found them reliable.

issues.definition: When an appeal from conviction involves reliable eyewitness accounts and a prompt report identifies a witness as present at the scene, the eyewitness testimony is accepted.

issues.legal_issue: A person cannot be held liable for another person’s murder on the basis of shared intention without evidence establishing a shared intention to commit that offence.
material_facts: One accused inflicted all the injuries on the deceased, including the fatal injuries.
The other accused persons were not shown to be armed or to have assaulted the deceased or exhorted the assailant.
The prosecution alleged generally that all the accused dragged the deceased from the train, but the evidence and circumstances did not establish prior concert or a meeting of minds.
issues.conclusion: The court held that the other accused persons could not be convicted of murder on the basis of shared intention and set aside their convictions for that offence.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code requires proof of a shared intention. The court found no evidence of prior concert or a meeting of minds, and cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: appeal_from_conviction and one_accused_inflicted_fatal_injuries and other_accused_unarmed and other_accused_did_not_assault_victim and no_exhortation_or_prior_concert_evidence and only_general_participation_alleged

predicates.appeal_from_conviction: The accused appealed from convictions entered by the lower courts.
predicates.one_accused_inflicted_fatal_injuries: The evidence attributed all injuries on the deceased, including the fatal injuries, to one accused.
predicates.other_accused_unarmed: The other accused persons were not shown to have been armed.
predicates.other_accused_did_not_assault_victim: The other accused persons were not shown to have assaulted the deceased.
predicates.no_exhortation_or_prior_concert_evidence: There was no evidence that the other accused persons exhorted the assailant or had agreed in advance to commit the attack.
predicates.only_general_participation_alleged: The allegation against the other accused persons was limited to a general act of participation without further evidence of a shared intention.

issues.definition: When one accused alone inflicts the fatal injuries and the remaining accused are not shown to be armed, to have assaulted the victim, or to have acted pursuant to a shared plan, shared intention to commit the murder is not established.

issues.legal_issue: A murder conviction may stand against the person whose responsibility for inflicting the fatal injuries is established by reliable evidence, even when shared intention with others is not proved.
material_facts: The eyewitness evidence against one accused was found reliable and compelling.
The deceased had multiple incised wounds and abrasions, all attributed to that accused.
The other accused persons were not shown to share his intention.
issues.conclusion: The court upheld the individual assailant’s murder conviction, converting it from a conviction with shared-intention liability to a conviction for murder simpliciter, and retained the life sentence.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code to the accused whose responsibility for the fatal assault was established. It cited no earlier cases.

predicates.appeal_from_conviction: The accused appealed from a conviction entered by the lower courts.
predicates.reliable_evidence_identifies_fatal_assai: Reliable evidence identified the accused as the person who inflicted the fatal assault.
predicates.fatal_injuries_attributed_to_that_assail: The fatal injuries were attributed to that accused.

issues.definition: When reliable evidence identifies an accused as the assailant who inflicted the fatal injuries, that accused is convicted of murder individually.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction for causing simple injuries in furtherance of a shared intention cannot stand when the evidence supporting the alleged injuries is vague and uncorroborated.
material_facts: A witness alleged that one accused struck him with a stick and that he also received fist blows.
The court found the evidence about the injuries vague and uncorroborated.
The conviction for causing those injuries had been entered against all the accused on a shared-intention basis.
issues.conclusion: The court set aside the convictions and sentences of all the accused for causing simple injuries in furtherance of a shared intention.
issues.legal_principle: The court held the evidence insufficient to sustain the conviction under Sections 323 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code because it was vague and uncorroborated. It cited no earlier cases.

predicates.appeal_from_conviction: The accused appealed from convictions entered by the lower courts.
predicates.injury_evidence_vague: The evidence describing the injuries and how they were caused was vague.
predicates.injury_evidence_uncorroborated: The evidence supporting the alleged injuries was not corroborated.

issues.definition: When an appeal from conviction concerns alleged simple injuries supported only by vague and uncorroborated evidence, the simple-injury conviction is set aside.
